subject: Life Skills
title: The Ivy Lee Method
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Ivy Lee Method usable.

hook.text: In 1918, productivity consultant Ivy Lee gave steel magnate Charles Schwab one idea. Schwab paid $25,000 for it.

buildup.text: The method: each evening list your six most important tasks for tomorrow. Number them in order of true priority.

discovery.text: Start with number one and work until it is done. Only then move to number two. No multitasking allowed.

twist.text: Unfinished tasks roll to the next day's list. This forces honesty about what you can actually accomplish.

climax.text: The power is in the constraint. Six tasks, strict order, one at a time. Simplicity is the system.

punchline.text: Six tasks. Strict order. No switching. Done.

quiz.question: What is the core rule of the Ivy Lee Method?
options: Complete as many tasks as possible each day
Work on one task at a time in strict priority order
Spend equal time on every task on your list
